securityReviewCheckpoint.enumerationResistance: Independently verified: unknown email, wrong password, missing credential, disabled user, and policy-invalid passwords all produce byte-identical status, headers and body. No session is written and no Set-Cookie is issued on any failure path. No password, digest, address, Prisma code, or stack reaches the client.
securityReviewCheckpoint.timingMitigationMeasured: Failed path with a policy-valid password took 324 ms against 348 ms for a real successful verification, so the committed decoy Argon2id digest is exercised on the failure path. This is not a constant-time claim: a policy-invalid password short-circuits before Argon2 symmetrically on both paths, database round trips are not equalised, and there is no throttling.
securityReviewCheckpoint.sessionSecurity: Exactly one session per successful login; token present only in Set-Cookie and absent from body, other headers and URL; PostgreSQL stores only the SHA-256 digest and no column contains the raw token; HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax in both environments; __Host- and Secure in production with no configuration able to disable it; no Domain; measured lifetime exactly 604800000 ms with cookie Max-Age matching; duplicate cookies fail closed; logout revokes only the presented session, preserves the original revocation timestamp on repeat, leaves other sessions valid, and clears the cookie with matching attributes.
securityReviewCheckpoint.originEnforcement: All ten disallowed Origin forms rejected with 403, including scheme, port and host differences, a suffix lookalike, a wildcard, a trailing slash, and four spoofed forwarded/Host/Referer headers. Query-supplied credentials and tokens are ignored: a logout driven by ?token= does not revoke, and /auth/me cannot be driven by a query token.
securityReviewCheckpoint.noCredentialedCors: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Credentials or Access-Control-Allow-Headers header is emitted.
securityReviewCheckpoint.logging: No console, Logger, stdout or stderr write exists in the authentication path. Nest runs with logger disabled and the Prisma client keeps logging off.
securityReviewCheckpoint.deploymentBoundary: Not deployed. Absence of rate limiting is documented as a blocker for public internet exposure in docs/security/AUTH_API.md, docs/architecture/SECURITY.md and project-state.json.
securityReviewCheckpoint.defectsFoundAndFixed: Three, all in test/state bookkeeping rather than product behaviour: the recorded unit total was corrected from 109 to 112; seven integration assertions that counted sessions globally were scoped to the test own fixtures after unrelated residue made them fail; a defect found earlier in the stage in the origin allowlist validation, the exception filter error-type matching, and the oversized-body status are all still fixed.

atomicity.transaction: Single prisma.$transaction covering all security-sensitive writes.
order: per-user advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock on a hash of the user id)
conditional token consumption matching only an unused, unexpired row
credential replacement by compare-and-swap on digest and passwordChangedAt
revocation of every unrevoked, unexpired session
atomicity.argon2OutsideTransaction: Hashing runs before the transaction opens so no connection is held across a 64 MiB allocation. A token that loses the race after hashing has written nothing.
atomicity.concurrentRedemption: Exactly one winner; the loser receives the generic invalid-token failure.

sessionRevocation.raceRootCause: SessionService.createSession inserted a session with no coordination, while reset replaced the credential and revoked sessions inside a transaction. A login that had already verified the old password could insert after the reset revocation statement, leaving a session authorised by a password that no longer existed.
sessionRevocation.invariant: A login authenticated with a password that a completed reset replaced must not create a usable session after that reset.

protocol.lock: pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(user_id, 0)), transaction-scoped, taken on the same transaction client that performs the protected writes
protocol.argon2OutsideLock: Deliberate. A 64 MiB three-iteration allocation must not run while holding the lock and must not serialise concurrent logins for one user.
protocol.revalidation: The login re-reads passwordChangedAt under the lock and refuses if it differs from the value observed at verification. Every replacement advances it strictly, so a change is unambiguous. The digest is never returned to the caller.

guarantees: Login commits before the reset: the reset revokes the session the login created.
Reset commits before the login: the login observes the advanced credential version and refuses with the generic authentication failure.
Either mid-transaction: the advisory lock forces one of those two orders.
Concurrent valid logins are serialised but all admitted, each with a distinct session.
Concurrent resets yield exactly one winner with no partial application.
A disabled account is rejected during the in-lock revalidation.
An aborted transaction rolls back the entire reset and releases the lock.
doesNotGuarantee: It does not cancel an HTTP request that was already authorized; revocation only affects subsequent validation.
It does not order recovery issuance against login, which is unnecessary because issuance never touches the credential.
It does not add any schema column.

evidence.coordination: Explicit latch parked at the seam between password verification and session insertion. No sleeps and no timing assumptions.
evidence.criticalTest: Asserts the stale login rejects with AUTHENTICATION_FAILED and that zero session rows exist for that user.
evidence.negativeControl: Temporarily disabling both the advisory lock and the in-lock revalidation makes the critical test fail, with the login resolving successfully. The test detects the vulnerability rather than passing vacuously.
evidence.repeatRuns: 21 passed on three consecutive runs with identical results.
casesCovered: login verified before reset, insert delayed until after reset
reset commits before a previously started login inserts
no deadlocks or lock leaks, including after an aborted transaction on a second connection
login and reset coordinated across two independent connection pools

remainingArchitecturalLimitations: Concurrent logins for one user serialise on the advisory lock for the duration of the in-transaction revalidation and insert. That section performs no Argon2id work, so the window is short, but it is a per-user serialisation point.

The lock is advisory, so it coordinates only writers that take it. Any future session-creation path must also participate; the single existing production path is covered and asserted by a regression test.

securityReviewCheckpoint.credentialVersionFinding: passwordChangedAt is PostgreSQL timestamp(3) and JavaScript Date is also millisecond, so the accepted previous+1 arithmetic is not truncated. However a credential row that is deleted and recreated can legitimately reuse a timestamp, so the timestamp is not a unique version counter. A live probe reproduced exactly that: delete and recreate the credential with a different password but the original passwordChangedAt, and the timestamp comparison alone passes while the digest has changed. The in-lock check was therefore strengthened to compare a SHA-256 fingerprint of the stored digest alongside the timestamp.
securityReviewCheckpoint.digestExposure: The Argon2id digest is never returned by verifyCredentialVersioned and never compared in the clear; a one-way SHA-256 fingerprint is returned instead and is never logged. A regression test asserts the stored digest does not appear anywhere in the value the caller receives.
securityReviewCheckpoint.lockKeyFinding: Password reset originally carried its own inline pg_advisory_xact_lock expression rather than the shared helper, duplicating the key derivation in two places where they could drift. It now calls the same helper, so the key exists in exactly one place.
securityReviewCheckpoint.advisoryLockVerified: Login and reset acquire the identical lock key on the same transaction client that performs their protected writes; Argon2id runs before the lock; credential revalidation, session insertion, credential replacement, and session revocation all occur under it; xact-scope releases on rollback; no process-local mutex is used; the accepted createSession signature is retained; and the requirement that future session-creation paths participate is documented.
negativeControls: Disabling the advisory lock and the revalidation makes the critical race test fail with the login resolving successfully.
Removing only the digest fingerprint while keeping the timestamp comparison makes two credential-version tests fail, including the recycled-timestamp case.

acceptedGuarantees.sharedAdvisoryLock: Login and password reset acquire the same transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(user_id, 0)) on the same transaction client that performs their protected writes. The key derivation exists in exactly one shared helper.
acceptedGuarantees.argon2OutsideLock: Argon2id verification runs outside the lock, so a 64 MiB three-iteration allocation is never held under it and concurrent logins are not serialised by hashing.
acceptedGuarantees.loginRevalidatesUnderLock: Login revalidates the credential under the lock before session creation, comparing both passwordChangedAt and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the stored digest. The digest itself is never returned and never logged.
acceptedGuarantees.atomicReset: Password replacement, recovery-token consumption, outstanding-token invalidation, and session revocation are atomic in one transaction: all commit or all roll back.
acceptedGuarantees.inflightRequestsNotCanceled: A password reset does not cancel an HTTP request that was already authorized. Revocation affects subsequent validation only.
acceptedGuarantees.broaderConcurrencyNotClaimed: No concurrency guarantee beyond the above is claimed.

unresolvedRisksConfirmedAtAcceptance.perUserLoginSerialization: Concurrent logins for one user serialise on the advisory lock for the in-transaction revalidation and insert. That section performs no Argon2id work, so the window is short, but it is a per-user serialisation point.
unresolvedRisksConfirmedAtAcceptance.advisoryLockScope: Advisory-lock coordination applies only to participating writers. Any future session-creation path must acquire the same lock.
unresolvedRisksConfirmedAtAcceptance.noProductionEmailProvider: No real mail provider is authorized or configured.
unresolvedRisksConfirmedAtAcceptance.recoveryUnavailableInProduction: API_PASSWORD_RECOVERY_DELIVERY_MODE defaults to disabled and development-only is refused under NODE_ENV=production, so recovery is not usable in production.
unresolvedRisksConfirmedAtAcceptance.recoveryEmailFlooding: Issuance is unbounded, so a known address can be flooded.
unresolvedRisksConfirmedAtAcceptance.tokenRequestAbuse: Each issuance supersedes earlier tokens, so repeated requests can invalidate a victim outstanding token.
unresolvedRisksConfirmedAtAcceptance.tokenBruteForce: Bounded only by 256-bit entropy and the 30-minute lifetime.
unresolvedRisksConfirmedAtAcceptance.argon2ResourceExhaustion: Both recovery endpoints and login can trigger a 64 MiB Argon2id operation and none is throttled. This is the most direct availability risk.
unresolvedRisksConfirmedAtAcceptance.noComprehensiveRateLimiting: Stage 2.6 owns rate limiting; none exists to reuse.

ciReliability.incidentError: TS6053: File 'packages/database/src/generated/prisma/client.ts' not found, with TS2307 for './generated/prisma/client.js'.
ciReliability.flakeEvidence: Hosted run 37859811782 on the identical commit passed, so this was an intermittent race rather than a deterministic failure.
ciReliability.rootCause: packages/database declared build and typecheck as "prisma generate && tsc ...", and turbo.json gave both only dependsOn ["^build"]. The ^ prefix orders a package dependencies, not its own tasks, so @tsms/database#build and @tsms/database:typecheck were scheduled in parallel. Both wrote packages/database/src/generated/prisma and one task tsc read the directory while the other rewrote it.
ciReliability.taskGraphBefore: @tsms/database#typecheck (prisma generate + tsc --noEmit) and @tsms/database#build (prisma generate + tsc) running in parallel, both writing src/generated/prisma
ciReliability.taskGraphAfter: @tsms/database#db:generate (prisma generate, cache false) is the sole writer; build and typecheck depend on it and only read its output
fix: packages/database build and typecheck scripts no longer invoke prisma; they only run tsc.
turbo.json adds a db:generate task with cache: false.
turbo.json build.dependsOn and typecheck.dependsOn now include db:generate alongside ^build.
turbo.json globalEnv now includes API_PASSWORD_RECOVERY_DELIVERY_MODE and API_PASSWORD_RECOVERY_URL_BASE, which were documented but missing from the cache key.
ciReliability.cachingRationale: db:generate is uncached deliberately. Generation costs roughly 150-400 ms, and an uncached task removes any chance of an incomplete or stale restored directory being treated as a successful generation, which is the property the incident was about.
ciReliability.developerErgonomicsChange: Direct package invocations such as pnpm --filter @tsms/database typecheck no longer generate the client first; pnpm db:generate must be run first. Documented in the package script notes and docs/architecture/DEPENDENCY_REVIEW.md.

regressionCoverage.style: structural assertions against turbo.json, package scripts, .gitignore and the Prisma schema
regressionCoverage.negativeControl: Reintroducing "prisma generate &&" into the database build script fails two of the assertions.

remainingLimitations: Turbo caching for build and typecheck is retained. Their inputs are git-tracked files only, and schema.prisma, prisma.config.ts and the Prisma version in package.json are all tracked, so a change to any of them changes the hash.
A direct package-level build or typecheck invocation now requires pnpm db:generate first. The supported root-level commands are unaffected.
ciReliability.resolutionNote: The correction is implemented and locally validated, but hosted CI has not yet run against it. The Stage 1 follow-up stays open until a hosted validate run passes on the maintenance commit.
